title: Cessna 206H Stationair — Emergency Procedures
description: Emergency and abnormal procedures checklist for the Cessna 206H Stationair (2000-present) with Continental IO-540 fuel-injected engine. Memory items are marked. The IO-540 is fuel-injected — no carburetor heat; alternate air induction applies instead. All numeric limits and airspeeds must come from the specific aircraft POH. This checklist supplements, but does not replace, recurrent emergency training.

source.notes: No manufacturer document consulted. Written from general familiarity with the type.

known_issues.description: Contains no airspeeds, power settings, fuel quantities or other limitations — must come from aircraft POH.
Equipment variations exist across this model/variant. Verify items against the specific aircraft before use.

rights.notes: Manufacturer POH remains under copyright. This file does not reproduce its wording or selection of items.

items.response: DO NOT TURN BACK TO RUNWAY AT LOW ALTITUDE; LAND ON BEST SURFACE WITHIN 30° OF RUNWAY HEADING
items.detail: The 206H has a large useful load and may accelerate slowly; commit early to stopping on the remaining runway rather than continuing a questionable takeoff.

items.text: If engine stops or seizure appears imminent — proceed to Engine Failure in Flight checklist

The Continental IO-540 is fuel-injected — there is no carburetor heat control. Induction system icing of the air inlet is possible in visible moisture combined with temperatures near freezing. This section addresses alternate air use in those conditions.
Symptoms — unexplained power loss or rough running in visible moisture or near-freezing temperatures
